newsitem.title: SPAIN: Mexican ex-prosecutor Chapa denied bail in Spain.
newsitem.headline: Mexican ex-prosecutor Chapa denied bail in Spain.

text.p: A former Mexican prosecutor accused of planting evidence in a murder investigation centering on the brother of ex-president Carlos Salinas de Gortari was denied bail on Saturday following his arrest in Madrid.

High Court Judge Carlos Divar ruled that Pablo Chapa Bezanilla, who was captured on Friday night, would stay in jail while Spanish authorities decide whether to extradite him to his homeland, Mexican embassy officials said.

Chapa was a special prosecutor in the controversial investigation and arrest of Raul Salinas, who has been held since 1995 on charges of murder and illegal enrichment. Raul Salinas has denied any wrongdoing.
The allegations against Chapa arose from the discovery of a human skeleton in late 1996 at Raul Salinas' Mexico City ranch.

Chapa oversaw the excavation of the bones and suggested they were those of a missing congressman who was wanted on charges of helping Raul Salinas to plan the 1994 assassination of Jose Francisco Ruiz Massieu, the secretary general of Mexico's ruling party.

But authorities later determined the skeleton belonged to a relative of a psychic who was reportedly helping Chapa with the investigation. Officials said it was dug up from a cemetery and buried at the ranch.
Chapa faced allegations that he arranged for the planting of the skeletal remains in an attempt to implicate Raul Salinas.

Chapa was fired from the attorney general's office in December 1996 and went into hiding earlier this year. In a letter published in Mexican newspapers in February, Chapa said he would wait until a "climate of lynching" calmed before he turned himself in.

The Mexican government declared him a fugitive and issued an international arrest warrent accusing him of criminal association, providing false information, violating burial laws and abusing his powers as a government official.
A joint investigation by Spanish and Mexican police led to his arrest Friday night, officials said.

According to Spanish news reports, Chapa had been living for several months in a chalet in the northern part of the city and was detained as he left a restaurant on the Plaza Mayor, one of Madrid's most popular tourist attractions.
